title: Move Notion pages with AI to the parent you choose
h1: put a notion page under its new parent
description: Ask a bot to move an existing Notion page under another page or into a database data source. Confirm both references before changing its location.
keywords: ai move notion page to database
answer: **put the finished brief where your team will look for it.** a bot moves an existing notion page under another page or into a database, keeping its contents intact. give it the source link and destination link. you get the original page in its new home, without a second copy to keep in sync.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: move the page, with a clear destination.
what:
**two pages called archive are a good reason to paste the link.** links settle which page moves and where it belongs. the bot can search notion by name to find candidates.

a database destination works differently from a parent page. say which you mean. the move changes the page’s home and leaves the writing alone.
uses: **file a finished event brief.** move it under the right annual archive.
**bring a stray note home.** place it in the agreed project database.
**repair the handbook’s structure.** move the onboarding page without rewriting it.

routine.message:
on the first friday of each month at 13:45, read event briefs under the events page i linked. find briefs whose event date has passed.

- show each source link and proposed destination under the linked archive
- ask me before you change anything
- move only the pages i choose

never move a database or rewrite a brief. never choose a destination from its title alone.
routine.when: first friday of the month at 13:45
routine.needs: notion connected with read and write; access to source pages and the destination
routine.output:
event briefs proposed for archive
rookhaven winter fair brief: event date passed
from: events
to: events archive / winter fairs
proposed move: this brief only, to the winter fairs archive.

steps: **allow a move deliberately.** connect notion with read and write for this bot.
**give both links.** say whether the destination is a page or database.
**approve the route.** ask the bot to show source and destination links before it moves the page.
**open its new home.** confirm the first brief is there. pause the routine when monthly filing is finished.
watch: **database moves need a database destination.** tell the bot if it treated one as a page.
**use links to tell copies apart.** open the source and destination before approving the route.
**make the bot wait for your go-ahead.** moves use write access and bypass the email sending setting. the routine above adds the pause.

faq.q: can it move a page into a database?
faq.a: **yes, give the database link.** the bot must use that database’s destination rather than treat it as a parent page.

faq.q: does moving also rewrite the contents?
faq.a: **no, this action relocates the page.** ask for any rewrite as a separate job.

steps: copy the destination link and say page or database
ask for a move preview without changing anything
open both links before allowing the move

worked.intro: invented example: felix files a finished event brief.
worked.before: the winter fair brief sits under events. two other pages also have "archive" in their names.
worked.after: felix gives the exact archive link. the bot shows the source and destination, waits, then moves only that brief.

mistakes.fix: paste the destination link so the bot can distinguish copies.

mistakes.mistake: expecting send approval to stop a move
mistakes.fix: require your go-ahead in the move request. sending approval covers a different action.

tip.text: a move should leave the writing alone. say so if you want filing rather than editing.
